prose_updates.tldr: For the unequal three-arm contrast \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), the unrestricted design--estimator game has the proved sharp expansion \(R_n(c^\dagger)=n^{-1}-C_A(5/8)^{2/3}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\). The contrast-weighted independent allocation \(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\) attains the same second-order coefficient, and the binary eight-type construction supplies a terminating finite-input certificate with a computable all-future error tail. An exact endpoint-reduction theorem also transports both the unrestricted three-arm result and the general fixed-independent benchmark to every fixed bounded interval \([L,U]\), multiplying risk by \(U-L)^2\). The bounded lift is mathematically total, but no exact Turing claim is made for unrepresented real endpoints or observations.

project_justification.gap: The two-arm literature solves the unrestricted binary-treatment action space, whereas it does not determine the sharp coefficient for three active arms. The proved three-arm allocation-tube theorem closes the formerly missing design-independent Bayes bridge for \(c^\dagger\), uniformly over local counts, exterior positive-count allocations, proper faces, dependent assignment laws, and randomized labeled-data estimators. The remaining mathematical gap is unrestricted sharpness for a general permitted multiarm contrast, not the fixed-independent expansion.
project_justification.niche: At \(c^\dagger\), the face-robust basis \([v,d^\dagger,\mathbf 1]\) separates target, transverse, and common-shift directions. Exact finite-population regression and directional van Trees bounds then control every allocation face, while the independent Airy feedback supplies the matching upper procedure. This yields the first sharp unrestricted three-active-arm coefficient in the note's fixed-horizon binary experiment and shows that \(q^\dagger\) has no second-order loss at this contrast.
project_justification.fill: The contribution consists of the proved eight-type face-robust all-count Bayes expansion, its lossless orbit reduction against arbitrary outcome-independent dependent designs and arbitrary randomized estimators, a matching total binary procedure, the evaluable Airy object \(C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\), and a terminating rational finite-data certificate with a nonincreasing computable tail. A separate exact bounded-endpoint reduction uses an observable finite Bernoulli polynomial and conditional Jensen, preserving the design and estimator quantifiers and multiplying both minimax risks and attaining bounds by \(U-L)^2\).

prose_updates.related_work: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026), Theorems 2.2--2.3 and 3.1, optimize over the same unrestricted assignment-mechanism and measurable-estimator quantifiers for a binary-treatment action space: they prove the exact binary game, exact bounded-endpoint scaling, and its Airy expansion. Hull (2026), Theorem 1, likewise optimizes over every assignment mechanism and measurable estimator and gives the equivalent exact bounded two-arm game. Neither result covers three arms. Restricting the present three-arm nature class by \(Y(2)=Y(3)\) gives the valid comparison \(R_n(c^\dagger)\ge\rho_n^\star=n^{-1}-C_A n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\). Since \(C_A>C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\), that imported two-arm converse is strictly weaker than the proved sharp three-arm coefficient. Hirano and Porter (2009) and Levit (1986) motivate limiting-decision and spectral arguments, while Bai (2023), Armstrong (2022), and Aronow and Lopatto (2026) study different restrictions. Hammer et al. (1996) supplies only prospective motivation for a complete fixed-horizon binary-endpoint regimen trial; no reanalysis of censored ACTG175 outcomes is claimed.
prose_updates.interpretation: For the planned binary three-regimen contrast \(c^\dagger\), a trialist may use \(q^\dagger\), the total Airy-feedback estimator, and the terminating finite-sample certificate knowing that their second-order value matches the unrestricted optimum even when competing designs may correlate assignments across units. For a bounded endpoint on a fixed real interval \([L,U]\), the observable Bernoulli-polynomial lift gives the same conclusion after multiplying squared risk by \(U-L)^2\). This bounded statement is mathematical rather than an exact-computation claim for arbitrary unrepresented reals.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Unrestricted sharpness is proved at the fixed rational contrast \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), not for every permitted multiarm contrast; accordingly, equality versus strict second-order loss of \(q^\star\) remains open in general. The effective binary certificate uses rational and ordered-algebraic input records, and no representation-independent terminating evaluator is claimed for an arbitrary real contrast, endpoint, or observed value. These are scope limits, not missing steps in the proved \(c^\dagger\) equality or in the exact bounded-risk scaling identity.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The unrestricted sharp theorem and its computable finite-data certificate concern the binary unequal three-arm contrast \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\). The exact endpoint reduction gives a mathematically total bounded-outcome corollary for every fixed real \(L<U\), and the fixed-independent bounded expansion holds for every permitted fixed contrast. The paper does not claim unrestricted sharpness for general \(c\) or a terminating evaluator for an arbitrary real contrast or unrepresented real bounded dataset. At \(c^\dagger\), however, the independent allocation \(q^\dagger\) is proved second-order optimal; the equality-versus-loss question remains open only beyond this established contrast.
